newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes firmer, Tapis indications firm.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes firmer, Tapis indications firm.

text.p: Asian crude prices were firmer on Wednesday in quiet trading but with firm market premiums being talked amid demand from China and Japan.
Traders said a wide Brent/Tapis spread was attracting West African grades to Asia -- with a VLCC of Bonny Light/Forcados into Yukong being talked.
However, the Brent/Dubai, assessed at $1.85/$1.93 for March was slightly offsetting wider sales to Asia.
China's buying for February was supporting Indonesia medium grades, including Minas, Widuri, which are both attracting premiums well above $1.00 per barrel.
One trader said China's interest to buy in February was not as high as January but sufficient to support the Widuri market. Minas dealers have reported similar sentiment.
Paper Tapis held steady with 50,000 barrels of February paper traded at $24.63 and 50,000 barrels of paper traded at $23.90, indicating a wide 70-cent spread.
A Tapis producer was heard already offering March barrels amid healthy demand for first half February and contributing to backwardation on the front-month spread on paper.
The firm Tapis market was further reflected by a deal in February Challis.
A producer sold 250,000 barrels of mid February Challis at Tapis quotes plus $2.60. That indicated an outright price of $27.25.
A trader sold a cargo of Belida to a major at ICP plus $1.20/$1.30.

A lifter of Griffin crude, who had already covered immediate needs with a fill-in crude owing to shipping delays after the latest cyclone, was said to be offering the Australian grade for second-half January loading. --Singapore, N. Fullick (+65 870 3081)
